extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering), spanning 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection took three stages: first, common university majors were screened based on the principle that visual inputs are commonly adopted to provide valuable information. Second, over 50 university students and co-authors specializing in these majors collected multimodal questions from major textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary, adhering to copyright and avoiding immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination. A total of 13K questions were initially gathered.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, and free online study resources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning was conducted in two main steps: lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to detect and eliminate duplicate problems; problems were then distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. Finally, problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded, leaving 11,550 questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions, multiple-choice options, correct answers, image types, difficulty levels, and explanations (where available) were annotated into structured JSON format by college student annotators and authors. Questions were classified as multiple-choice or open-ended, and images were inserted as file paths in the question, options, or explanations. Ambiguous cases were flagged and reviewed in team meetings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed specifically for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects specializing in the relevant majors.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Discusses monitoring progress towards Level 3 / Expert AGI ('at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' in broad tasks), which marks a substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor, carrying significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for fully testing Expert AGI, as there lacks a direct mapping between MMMU performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI must tackle.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models (LMMs) and foundation models on college-level perception, domain-specific knowledge recall, and complex multi-discipline reasoning. Divided into a few-shot development set (150 questions), validation set (900 questions for hyperparameter selection), and test set (10,500 questions).
